messages.author: 93fdeb4704061276
messages.subject: Terminology
parts:
Hi. I found this while searching for something else. I think you have some interesting approaches here, but your docs are tough to understand sometimes because you dont always define terminology and sometimes you invent new terms for common R things. I wonder if other visitors react same way.

Example. Argument 'to_predict' is a puzzler. If you name that 'newdata' then you will be immediately understood by R users of the predict() function.

Example. You use symbol Ss. Why not define it?

Example. Instructions use term '.()' list, but don't define. Maybe its just me, but until terms like that go into base R, you ought to define or give link to explanation.

I wonder if your ideas about making an easy way to estimate simulated predictions (you call boot) can be distinguished from the effort in other projects to do same. See Zelig, for example, which does same for a laundry list of regression models.

It would help me if you explained more about what you are sampling. The design matrix is fixed, but param estimates are MVN? I'm not entirely sure most people would call that bootstrap. But it is simulation. Maybe I'm wasting time on distinction here. Look at how they describe in the Zelig docs, for example. Your warning about bogus cell estimates when intercept is not fixed is curious and thought provoking. If other people who simulate predicted values did not address same issue, then maybe you can focus attention there.

Now that the release version of lme4 has a predict method, perhaps you can distinguish from that. I don't see your idea as easier. I agree you did need that function before summer, 2013. Not now, though.

Many of us have worked on these same problems, its funny how answers tend in same direction. We start out trying to simplify an an R usage and we end up with a new thing that is not simpler than base R. Just different. Like you, I found it much more difficult to manage continuous predictors in newdata construction. Its very tough to know if a model written like

d <- 4
lm(y ~ x1 + log(x2 + d))

Will come through the prediction process as the user intends. That requires some programming effort...

One last thing. Why your documents have this style?

, arg = val
, arg = val
??

Is that suggested in another language? I've never seem anywhere else.

Paul Johnson
http://pj.freefaculty.org
